boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Kingston-campus places documented by URI for studying, meeting, student organizations, recreation, and campus programs.

cards.title: Memorial Student Union
cards.subtitle: Student groups, services, and a between-class pause
cards.notes: Use the Union as a practical meet-up point: it houses student groups and involvement offices, and includes space to relax or play pool.
cards.short_summary: A staffed student-life hub with room for meetings and downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: URI says the Memorial Student Union is home to more than 120 student groups and several student-support offices, with places to relax or play pool.
cards.source_title: Resources for Students – Memorial Student Union
cards.access_notes: Check the Union’s current building access and room schedules before planning a group meeting.

cards.title: The Quad
cards.subtitle: Kingston campus outdoor event space
cards.notes: Walk through the Quad between classes, or reserve it through the student-event process when your registered organization is planning a program.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed lawn that URI includes in its student-event booking process.
cards.evidence_claim: URI’s student-event guidance specifically lists the Quad among spaces that organizations can reserve before registering an in-person event.
cards.access_notes: Organization events require an approved space reservation and event registration; use it casually only in accordance with posted rules.

cards.title: Multicultural Student Services Center
cards.subtitle: 74 Lower College Road
cards.notes: Stop in during open hours for a campus community space, or ask about reserving the Hardge Forum for an eligible group program.
cards.short_summary: A campus community center with a reservable multipurpose forum.
cards.evidence_claim: URI identifies the MSSC at 74 Lower College Road and says its Hardge Forum is available to the wider campus community, with priority for specified organizations.
cards.source_title: Room Reservations – Multicultural Student Services Center
cards.access_notes: The cited URI page lists academic-year building hours of 8:30 a.m.–9 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Friday; confirm before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Robert L. Carothers Library and Learning Commons
cards.title: Carothers Library and Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Library study and academic-support hub
cards.notes: Choose the Learning Commons for a focused work session, then use the directory to locate research help, circulation, technology help, or other services.
cards.short_summary: The central library’s named first-floor academic workspace.
cards.evidence_claim: URI’s building directory lists the Learning Commons, Research Help Desk, Circulation, ITS Help Desk, and other student-facing services in Carothers Library.
cards.source_title: Robert L. Carothers Library & Learning Commons Building Directory
cards.access_notes: Library access and service availability can vary; consult the library before a planned visit.

cards.title: 24-Hour Study Room
cards.subtitle: Carothers Library, first floor
cards.notes: For a late study session, enter through the library before closing or use your URI ID at the designated brown-door card-swipe entrance afterward.
cards.short_summary: An academic-year overnight study option inside Carothers Library.
cards.evidence_claim: URI says the 24-Hour Study Room is open every night during the academic year, including weekends, with URI-ID card-swipe access after 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Late night: URI states it is open every night in the academic year; after 11 p.m., expect to use a URI ID at the brown-door card swipe.

cards.title: Carothers Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lower Level and floors 1–3
cards.notes: Reserve a group study room through the library’s booking system when your team needs a defined place to talk through work together.
cards.short_summary: Reservable collaborative rooms distributed across the Kingston library.
cards.evidence_claim: URI says group study rooms are on the Lower Level and floors 1 through 3 of the Kingston University Library and can be reserved online.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required through the library booking system; room availability and access rules may vary.

cards.title: MakerspaceURI
cards.subtitle: Carothers Library, Room 165
cards.notes: Find MakerspaceURI in Room 165 when your project needs a named library-based making space; verify current services before bringing materials.
cards.short_summary: A designated makerspace located inside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: URI’s Carothers Library directory lists MakerspaceURI in Room 165 on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Robert L. Carothers Library & Learning Commons Building Directory
cards.access_notes: Confirm current makerspace hours, equipment access, and any project requirements with the library.

cards.title: Launch Lab
cards.subtitle: Carothers Library, Room 104
cards.notes: Use the building directory to locate the Launch Lab in Room 104, then check with its host program for current access or programming.
cards.short_summary: A named first-floor lab within Carothers Library.
cards.evidence_claim: URI’s Carothers Library directory lists the Launch Lab in Room 104 on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Robert L. Carothers Library & Learning Commons Building Directory
cards.access_notes: Confirm current access, hours, and program eligibility before relying on the space.

cards.title: Ranger Hall Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Ranger Hall campus anchor option
cards.notes: Try the study spaces in Ranger Hall as a regular daytime anchor, especially when you need a defined campus place between work and classes.
cards.short_summary: A student-affairs-listed study option beyond the central library.
cards.evidence_claim: URI Commuter Affairs includes labs and study spaces in Ranger Hall among examples of campus places students can choose as a reliable anchor.
cards.access_notes: Check building access and any room-specific rules before settling in.

cards.title: Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: Campus anchor for commuter students
cards.notes: If you commute, consider the Commuter Lounge as a regular reset point for studying, meeting friends, or filling time between commitments.
cards.short_summary: A URI-listed anchor space for students balancing campus with off-campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: URI Commuter Affairs identifies the Commuter Lounge as one of the campus places students can use as a reliable study, hangout, or meeting anchor.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the lounge’s current location, access conditions, and hours through Commuter Affairs.
